title: Is Buy Now Pay Later Actually a Debt Trap for Young Indians?

content:
Buy now pay later isn't a scam. It isn't automatically dangerous, either. Used for one predictable monthly expense with a clear 15-day repayment window, it's a credit tool that costs you nothing. Used across three apps for impulse buys, it becomes the kind of debt that's easy to forget until your CIBIL score takes the hit.

About 30% of Indian BNPL users report struggling to repay on time. That's not a fringe number. The product works for the 70% who use it carefully, and poorly for the third who don't.

Key Takeaways

  • About 30% of Indian BNPL users report difficulty repaying on time, per financial surveys.
  • Missing a payment by one day can trigger late fees and a CIBIL score drop.
  • The real risk is fragmented debt: running multiple BNPL apps makes your total borrowing invisible.
  • BNPL works for predictable, already-budgeted expenses, not impulse purchases.
  • RBI tightened BNPL oversight in 2025-26, requiring weekly credit bureau reporting from all lenders.

How the 15-Day Repayment Window Actually Works

Most Indian BNPL apps, including Simpl and LazyPay, give you exactly 15 days to repay the full amount. There's no interest if you pay on time. But if your salary arrives at month-end and the repayment falls mid-cycle, you'll miss the window even with money incoming.

Say you've got a 2,500 rupee jacket in your Myntra cart. You tap Pay Later using Simpl. The money isn't yours. It's a short-term loan. If your paycheck lands on the 28th and the BNPL due date falls on the 15th, you'll be short despite having money coming. That's the scenario that trips up most first-time users in month one.

The cost most articles gloss over: late fees on Indian BNPL apps typically run between 100 and 500 rupees per transaction, regardless of the original amount. A 500 rupee purchase that goes five days overdue can incur a 150 rupee penalty. That's effectively 30% on a five-day delay. The apps don't advertise this prominently, and most users don't read the fine print untill after the first penalty charge lands.

LazyPay vs. Simpl vs. Flipkart Pay Later: Key Differences

All three operate under RBI's digital lending framework, but the terms vary in ways that matter when something goes wrong:

FeatureLazyPaySimplFlipkart Pay Later
Credit limitUp to 1,00,000 rupeesMerchant-linkedUp to 1,00,000 rupees
Repayment window15 days15 days30 days (monthly)
Typical late fee100 to 500 rupeesPlatform-specific2% per month on outstanding
Reports to CIBILYesYesYes

Flipkart Pay Later's 30-day window is more forgiving if your salary arrives monthly. LazyPay and Simpl work fine for frequent small purchases, but their 15-day cycles mean repayment lands before the next paycheck for anyone buying mid-month.

When Does BNPL Actually Hurt Your CIBIL Score?

BNPL hurts your CIBIL score when you miss a payment, not just from using it. Under RBI's 2025-26 guidelines, all BNPL lenders must report to credit bureaus weekly. A single missed payment can appear on your report within days, fast enough to affect loan applications already in progress.

That's new. Until recently, several BNPL apps didn't report to CIBIL at all. That was quietly a selling point. Now they do, and the change matters most for people in their early 20s building a credit history from scratch.

A 2026 research paper on India's BNPL market noted that young borrowers are defaulting early in their earning careers, damaging credit histories before they fully understand what credit means. Something similar has occured in other markets when BNPL regulation tightened: the users most drawn to these products were also the least prepared for the credit consequences.

The Fragmented Debt Problem Nobody Talks About

This is probably the biggest real risk, and almost no mainstream personal finance content discusses it clearly.

When repayment schedules are seperate and untracked across multiple platforms, the total debt stops feeling like a real obligation. If you use Simpl for groceries, LazyPay for clothing, Flipkart Pay Later for electronics, and Amazon Pay Later for gadgets, you have four different due dates, four penalty structures, and four notification systems that don't talk to each other. Your bank account looks fine. Your day-to-day spending feels normal.

Then you apply for a personal loan and find five open credit lines in your CIBIL report that you'd mentally filed as just apps. The credit inquiry drops your score slightly. The open BNPL balances reduce your available credit headroom. The lender gets nervous about the scattered debt picture. None of this is visible until you need something that actually matters.

Should You Use BNPL for Everyday Spending in India?

BNPL is genuinely useful for specific situations and a poor fit for most others. Used for predictable, budgeted expenses where you know the exact repayment date, it's free credit. Used for impulse buys mid-month without a clear repayment plan, it accumulates faster than most users expect.

  • Use it when you know the exact date you'll repay, tied to a salary or fixed income date.
  • Stick to one purchase on one platform, not multiple purchases spread across several apps.
  • Keep the purchase under 5% of your monthly take-home so a missed payment won't strain your finances.
  • Read the penalty terms for that specific app before the first purchase, not after the first charge.

BNPL is built to reduce what researchers call the pain of payment. Making spending feel less real is the feature, not a flaw. Knowing this won't make you immune to it. But it changes how you use the checkout screen.

This post describes how BNPL products generally work in India. It is general financial information, not personal financial advice.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does using BNPL hurt your credit score automatically?

No, simply using BNPL doesn't affect your score. Only missed or late payments reported to CIBIL do. Since 2025-26, all RBI-regulated BNPL lenders must report credit activity weekly, so any default shows up on your report within days.

What happens if I miss a BNPL payment in India?

Late fees apply immediately, typically 100 to 500 rupees depending on the platform. After a few days, the overdue balance gets reported to credit bureaus. Continued non-payment leads to collection processes under RBI's digital lending rules, which can include formal legal recovery.

Can BNPL help me build a credit score in India?

Yes, if you repay on time consistently. On-time payments appear as positive credit history in your CIBIL report. The catch is the 15-day window is short, and a single slip has the opposite effect compared to several months of on-time behavior.

Should I use more than one BNPL app at the same time?

I'd avoid it. Tracking multiple repayment cycles and due dates across different apps is genuinely harder than it sounds. One missed payment from a forgotten app can damage your credit score for months and complicate future loan applications.

Is Simpl safe for everyday grocery purchases in India?

Simpl is fine for regular, budgeted purchases you'd make anyway. The risk comes from using it as a substitute for money you don't yet have. A useful rule: if you wouldn't buy it with your debit card right now, don't put it on BNPL.

The Short Version

BNPL isn't a trap by design. It becomes one when spending feels free and repayment feels like a future problem. Used for one purchase at a time, with a clear repayment date in mind, it's a functional tool. Used across multiple apps for impulse buys, it quietly builds debt in several places until the CIBIL check for your first home or personal loan makes it all visible at once.
